prompt: Clause 7.2 of the ORASHI register has nothing recorded. A request sets it to Conformant and supplies an evidence reference, with no assessment date and no assessor. What does canSetClauseStatus answer?
options: It allows the status, because the evidence reference is what a conformity claim stands on.
It refuses, in the same sentence it gives a Conformant request that carries nothing at all.
It refuses with the shorter sentence asking only for the date and the assessor.
It allows the status and lists 7.2 under missingEvidenceParts for the rest.
explanation: The course prints REFUSED for Conformant with an evidence reference only, in the words it uses for Conformant with nothing else: name the evidence, the date it was assessed and who assessed it. The shorter sentence belongs to a Nonconformant request with no date.

prompt: Clause 7.2 has nothing recorded. Which of these requests on it does canSetClauseStatus ALLOW?
options: Compliant, which is a word the clause status vocabulary does not carry.
Partially conformant, with nothing else recorded on the clause.
Not applicable as its status, while its applicability still reads Applicable.
Nonconformant, with the date it was assessed and the assessor.
explanation: Nonconformant with a date and an assessor: ALLOWED. Partially conformant with nothing else is refused and asks for evidence as well. Not applicable while the clause still reads Applicable is refused because the two fields move together. Compliant is not a clause status.

prompt: A request sets clause 7.2's status to Not applicable while its applicability still reads Applicable. Which requirement stops it?
options: The applicability and the status are set together, or neither is.
An excluded clause keeps its justification on record.
Every verdict names the evidence, the date it was assessed and who assessed it before it stands.
Not applicable is a word the clause vocabulary does not carry, so the status itself is refused.
explanation: The refusal reads: "A clause determined not applicable cannot also carry a conformity verdict. Set both together, or neither." The justification rule arises once both fields read Not applicable, and Not applicable is one of the five words in CLAUSE_STATUSES.

prompt: Both fields of a clause are set to Not applicable with no justification. Of the four refusals the course prints for this request, which one cites a numbered clause of the standard?
options: The ISO 14001:2015 refusal, which cites §9.2 of the standard the ORASHI register is kept against.
The ISO 45001:2018 refusal, which cites §4.3 in the same words the ISO 9001:2015 sentence uses.
The ISO 9001:2015 refusal, which cites §4.3 of that standard.
The no-standard refusal, which falls back to §4.3.
explanation: Only the ISO 9001:2015 sentence names §4.3. The ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 sentences name their standard in the engine's own shape, and with no standard passed the sentence names none. All four are refusals.

prompt: The same Not applicable request, with no justification, is sent with no standard passed as the fourth argument. What comes back?
options: An allowed verdict, because without a standard there is no requirement left to justify.
A refusal naming ISO 14001:2015, the standard of the register the clause sits in.
A refusal that asks why the requirement does not apply and names no standard.
A refusal saying the call is missing its standard, returned before any justification is read.
explanation: The course prints: "Say why this requirement does not apply. A requirement determined not applicable keeps its justification on record." The verdict is the same refusal for all three standards and for none; only the wording follows the standard passed.

prompt: Asked to set clause 7.2 to Compliant, the gate answers "Compliant is not a clause status." Where does the word Compliant belong in this course?
options: In the clause register, as a Conformant claim's word once evidenced.
In the obligation register, where it is one of the complianceStatus words.
In the readiness counts, as the count of conformant clauses.
In the document library, as the state of a document in force.
explanation: complianceStatus.STATUS_SEVERITY carries Compliant. isoCompliance.CLAUSE_STATUSES holds Not assessed, Conformant, Partially conformant, Nonconformant and Not applicable, and the readiness count is named conformant. Each register is held to its own vocabulary.

prompt: Clause 5.2 reads Conformant, claims conformity true, evidence record false and assessed true. What does missingEvidenceParts print for it?
options: evidence reference
evidence reference, the date assessed and the assessor
nothing, because the row already reads assessed true
no row, since it lists Nonconformant clauses only
explanation: missingEvidenceParts covers each applicable clause that claims conformity without a complete record, and prints 5.2: evidence reference. Its assessed column reads true, so the date and the assessor are there.

prompt: Clause 6.1.3 reads Nonconformant, with evidence record false and assessed true. What does that row show about the gate?
options: The row could not have passed the gate, since every clause verdict needs an evidence reference.
The row is the unevidenced claim the register summary counts, because its evidence record reads false.
The row is waiting on an assessor, since assessed marks only the date.
The verdict carries what the gate asks of it: a date and an assessor, with no evidence reference.
explanation: A Nonconformant status needs two of the three. Clause 6.1.3 reads claims conformity false, so it makes no claim, and the summary's unevidenced claims 1 is clause 5.2.

prompt: Clause 4.3 reads Conformant and review overdue true on the same row at 2026-10-15. What do the two readings say together?
options: The Conformant verdict lapses to Not assessed once the clause's next review date has passed.
The status column prints Review overdue in place of Conformant until the review is recorded.
The overdue flag is held back while the clause reads Conformant.
The last verdict still stands, and it is due to be looked at again and has not been.
explanation: Clause 4.3's next review, 2026-10-01, is -14 days from the as-of date. The status is the last verdict and the flag says its review is late; neither changes the other. Review overdue is a Document Control review state.

prompt: At 2026-10-15 clause 6.1.2's next review is 2026-11-02, 18 days away. Which flags does the engine print for it?
options: review due soon true, and review overdue true
review due soon true, and review overdue false
review overdue true, and review due soon false
both false, as the date is ahead of the as-of date
explanation: 18 days sits inside the window isoCompliance.REVIEW_LEAD_DAYS sets, and the date is ahead of the as-of date. No ORASHI row reads true for both flags, and 6.1.2 is the one clause that reads review due soon true.

prompt: Clause 4.4, the excluded clause, has no next review date. What do its two review flags read?
options: review overdue true, because a review date that is missing is treated as one that has passed.
review due soon true, because a missing date is read as falling inside the lead window.
Both false, and 4.4 is left out of the clause review table.
Neither prints, and the summary counts 4.4 among reviews overdue.
explanation: The register prints next review none, review overdue false and review due soon false for 4.4, whose applicability and status both read Not applicable, and the table of clause reviews against the as-of date lists the other 12 clauses without it. The summary's reviews overdue 1 is clause 4.3.

prompt: The summary prints reviews overdue 1 and reviews due soon 1. Which of the two does the readiness list carry, and at which severity?
options: Only the overdue review, as the watch item "1 clause review is past due."
Both, as two watch items, one for each review flag.
Only the overdue review, as a serious item.
Neither, since readiness does not read clause reviews.
explanation: The list carries one watch item for reviews and none for clause 6.1.2's review due soon. The serious item on clause 4.3 is its stale coverage, a separate question asked of the same row.

prompt: The register summary prints evidenced claims 9 and unevidenced claims 1. Which clause is the one unevidenced claim?
options: Clause 6.1.3, Compliance obligations
Clause 5.2, Environmental policy
Clause 7.2, Competence
Clause 4.4, the excluded clause
explanation: An unevidenced claim claims conformity without its evidence record. Clauses 6.1.3 and 7.2 both read evidence record false, and neither claims conformity; 4.4 is excluded. Only 5.2 reads claims conformity true beside evidence record false.

prompt: Partially conformant sits between Conformant and Nonconformant. Which of the two does it match on what canSetClauseStatus asks for?
options: Conformant: it is refused without evidence, a date and an assessor, in the same sentence.
Nonconformant: a date and an assessor are enough, and no evidence reference is asked for.
Neither: it needs an evidence reference alone, since a partial claim carries no assessment.
Neither: it is refused unless the clause's applicability is changed in the same request.
explanation: The course prints Partially conformant, nothing else: REFUSED, with the sentence Conformant meets, and ALLOWED with evidence, a date and an assessor. Clause 6.1.2 reads Partially conformant with claims conformity, evidence record and assessed all true.

prompt: The readiness counts print evidenced 9 and conformant 9. Do the two counts cover the same nine clauses?
options: Yes. Every Conformant clause carries evidence, so the two counts are one set of clauses.
No. The evidenced count takes in the excluded clause 4.4, which the conformant count leaves out.
Yes. The evidenced count is taken over the Conformant clauses only, so it cannot differ.
No. Clause 5.2 is Conformant without evidence, and clause 6.1.2 is evidenced without being Conformant.
explanation: Conformant rows: 4.1, 4.3, 5.2, 7.5.3, 8.1, 8.2, 9.1.1, 9.2 and 10.2. Evidence record true: the same list with 6.1.2 in place of 5.2, and 4.4 reads false. Two equal counts need not be one set, which is why a report quotes each as it prints.
